clue.text: It's said to push between opposites

indicators.note: between tells us the push word sits inside the pair of opposite letters

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are opposite compass points
to poke is to push or prod

explanation.surface: Someone is told to push their way between two opposing parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken is uttered aloud, which is exactly what it means for a thing to be said.

clue.text: Forward in 10, diverted to the point

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky
taken as written

indicators.note: diverted says the letters of the number are turned into a new order

parts.note: 10 is read as the number ten, not as the cross-reference

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark in the maintenance entry is diverted towards relevance.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to 10-down, but it simply means the number TEN, whose letters are rearranged to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant, bearing directly on the matter, which is being to the point.

clue.text: Drum makes the English rebel against the French

parts.note: Robert ... a rebellion in Norfolk against enclosures in 1549
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A drummer boy turns an English rebel against France.
explanation.walkthrough: A kettle is a kettledrum, the orchestral timpani.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle drum, or timpano, is a large bowl-shaped drum, often just called a kettle.

clue.text: 90-ton structure that doesn't exist?

definitions.note: the clause describes a thing; the answer is a noun for such a thing

indicators.note: structure means the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: 90 written out in words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ninety-ton building that somehow isn't there.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity is literally a non-being, something without real existence.

clue.text: Great guy with guns at hand

parts.note: gats is old American slang for pistols
by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: A fine fellow who keeps his firearms within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great guy' sounds like praise, but it points to the title character of The Great Gatsby, Fitzgerald's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the hero of the novel The Great Gatsby, so he is literally the 'Great' man of the title.

clue.text: Soldier obtained leg of mutton

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A soldier got hold of a joint of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigot is a culinary term, from French, for a leg of lamb or mutton.

clue.text: See 26
One old Jewish king backed more modern faith

indicators.note: backed means the pieces are read in reverse order, back to front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ahab was a king of Israel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A biblical king supported a newer religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baha'i faith was founded in 19th-century Persia, more modern than the old biblical religion.

clue.text: Container containing pupil Tories at the Ritz?

indicators.note: containing says the box word holds the pupil's letter inside it

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard container
L stands for learner, a pupil driver

explanation.surface: A box holding a schoolchild, and Conservatives dining at a smart London hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carlton Club is the oldest Conservative club in London, and the Ritz-Carlton is a hotel chain, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carlton Club is the Tories' traditional London club, and Ritz-Carlton links the name to the Ritz.

clue.text: Exposed to disrepute for having made mutual concessions

definitions.meaning: brought into danger or disgrace, as a reputation can be
settled by both sides giving ground in a deal

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both settling by concessions and placing someone's honour at risk.

clue.text: Lawman and schoolman coming good about fake

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sham is a fake

explanation.surface: A policeman and a teacher who turn out to be good after a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Gresham gave his name to Gresham's Law (bad money drives out good) and founded Gresham College; Gresham's is also an English school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor financier Thomas Gresham named an economic law and founded educational institutions, so he is both lawman and schoolman.

clue.text: See 26
Dressed, with mother around at little places like 19

indicators.note: around says the mother word wraps itself about the dressed word

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, a familiar British school term
soldiers who dress ranks stand in line
mini means little

explanation.surface: A child is dressed and fussed over by mother at some tiny destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is EUSTON, a big London railway terminus; 'dressed' is the drill-ground sense of lining up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of London's major railway terminals, an example of the large stations where main routes end.

clue.text: Hazard to sailors taken in when it's blowy

definitions.meaning: a ridge of rock or sand just below the sea's surface that wrecks ships
the portion of sail gathered in to shorten sail in a strong wind

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rocky ridge near the surface and the part of a sail rolled up in high wind.

clue.text: Strikers going round pit take a dip

indicators.note: going round says the strikers word encloses the pit word

parts.note: a picket is a group of strikers outside a workplace
a pock is a small pit or hollow in the skin

explanation.surface: Striking workers circle a coal mine before going for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests hitters, but it means a picket line; 'take a dip' suggests swimming, but a dip is slang for a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Dip is old slang for a petty thief who steals from people's pockets.

clue.text: King attacked Hitler with love at last and some frequency

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: attacked says the name is torn apart and rebuilt

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
Z comes at last in the alphabet, from A to Z

explanation.surface: A monarch fought the dictator, finally with affection, on some radio wavelength.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilohertz is a unit of frequency equal to a thousand cycles per second.

clue.text: Know big cat's name to be St Mungo

parts.note: ken is a Scots word for know
a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: Learn a big cat's name and it turns out to be Glasgow's saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Mungo, patron saint of Glasgow, is also known as Kentigern.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentigern is the formal name of the Glasgow patron saint whose pet name was Mungo.

clue.text: Generate new drink

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word are made afresh in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Produce a fresh beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a drink brewed from unfermented tea leaves.

clue.text: See 26
A negative available presently

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for negative
on means available, as in 'on offer'

explanation.surface: A refusal that will be available shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for soon, which is what presently means in British usage.

clue.text: American in school in London

definitions.note: the phrase describes a place; the answer names one

indicators.note: in says the American goes inside the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An American pupil at a school in London.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a London railway station and district; Eton itself is near Windsor, not in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is an area of central London, best known for its railway terminus.

clue.text: Fountain tee shot smashed, in the President's words

indicators.note: smashed tells us the letters of the golf phrase are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A golf drive off the tee hits a fountain, and the President comments on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'smashed' fits a golf shot that breaks something.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual address the US President gives to Congress is his set speech, in his own words.

clue.text: Report of what happened to Lucifer, the biggest in the world

definitions.text: Report of what happened to Lucifer
definitions.meaning: a headline saying the rebel archangel tumbles from heaven
the world's highest waterfall, in Venezuela

explanation.definitionFit: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the highest waterfall on Earth, and Lucifer was a fallen angel.

clue.text: See 21
A fool in face of modern technology?

indicators.note: in says the fool word goes inside the face word

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
git is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot as the public face of modern technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital describes computer-based modern technology, as opposed to analogue.

clue.text: Mystic symbol including the Ukrainian

indicators.note: including says the mystic symbol holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet credited with magic power
taken as written

explanation.surface: A magical sign worn by someone from Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ruthene is a Ruthenian, a member of an East Slavic people of western Ukraine.

clue.text: Almost every method is for good

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: all means every
a way is a method
S is the contraction of is, as in it's

explanation.surface: Nearly every approach is for the best.
explanation.definitionFit: For good means permanently, forever, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Harem without a doubt (first and last and centre): come fly to chaos, keeping killer now endlessly in French and English church with cult work of the '70s

indicators.note: without says the single letter a is taken away from the harem word

parts.note: a zenana is the women's quarters of a house in India, a harem

indicators.note: first and last picks the outer letters of the word doubt

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: keeping says the shuffled letters hold the killer inside
chaos, as where the fly comes to, means the letters of come fly to are thrown into disorder

parts.note: an orc, or killer whale, is a killer

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: maintenant is French for now, as the words in French signal
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A harem, a doubt, a fly come to chaos, a killer, French and an English church make up a whimsical 1970s cult book.
explanation.walkthrough: A typical Araucaria long composite clue. 'in French' tells you the word for now is French, and the anagram of COME FLY TO gives OFMOTYCLE before the killer goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Pirsig's 1974 philosophical novel became a cult book of the seventies.
